carrier_shape_decision.pinned_shape: Annotation.args (Vec<Spanned<AnnotationArg>>) for @optimization_log is a FLAT list where each element is EITHER (1) AnnotationArg::Record{fields} holding a block-level scalar (currently only `version`), held DIRECTLY (not Call-wrapped), OR (2) AnnotationArg::Call{name:"entry", args:[Record{fields}]} — one entry{...} declaration, Call-wrapped so downstream match arms stay uniform with @strategy's Call-wrapped hole declarations (matches AT-2900's literal wording). RecordField.value is the CLOSED RecordValue{Str|Int|Ident} enum (no Record/Call/Hole variant), so nesting is structurally impossible at exactly one level below Annotation.args.

known_limitations: Block-level `forward_unknown` (OptimizationLog.forward_unknown) is unreachable via this compiler's own parser today: §1.3a's EBNF pins block_item := version_field | entry_block as CLOSED, so no source-text block-level key other than `version` can ever be produced by parse_optimization_log_block. The HIR validator's block-level preserve-and-warn logic is exercised only via direct Rust-level RecordField construction (opt_log.rs unit tests), not through real parsed source -- it is forward-looking infrastructure for a FUTURE parser version that extends block_item. Entry-level forward_unknown IS reachable via real source today (field := ident ":" record_value admits any key) and is exercised end-to-end (AT-2925). Documented in opt_log.rs's forward_unknown field doc comment and DESIGN.md §3.1.43.

[RETRACTED, QA-fix pass, run M319-20260714-1400 continuation] The original text of this entry claimed reviewer resolution (b) could be skipped because 'no real source can carry a block-level version>1 today via this parser's own grammar'. QA (M3.19-qa.json top_priority_finding_deviation_2) built a real, hand-authored `@optimization_log { version: 2, entry {...} }` source, ran it through the real parser + `axc verify` + `axc compile`: it parses and lowers with ZERO errors, and is real, on-disk, HIR-valid source. QA then ran the real `axc log-opt` writer against it and it silently spliced a v1-shaped entry into the v2 block (exit 0, no warning) -- exactly the schema-version-mixing risk the pessimistic reviewer flagged. The original claim was FALSE: it conflated two different things -- 'an unknown BLOCK-LEVEL KEY is unreachable' (TRUE; §1.3a's EBNF pins `block_item := version_field | entry_block` closed, so no key OTHER than `version` can appear at block scope) with 'a block-level VERSION NUMBER greater than 1 is unreachable' (FALSE; `version` is always a plain, parseable, HIR-valid field -- §1.4a's own forward-compat design means version > SUPPORTED_OPT_LOG_VERSION is preserve-and-warn, not reject, so it compiles clean by design). FIX (this pass): added `LogOptError::UnsupportedVersion { found, supported }` to `crates/axc-driver/src/log_opt.rs`. `splice_optimization_log_entry` -- the ONE shared splice core used by both `axc log-opt` (CLI, via `append_optimization_log`) and the `append_optimization_log` MCP tool (`crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/append_optimization_log.rs`, which calls the same `append_optimization_log` function) -- now checks the existing block's HIR-validated `version` field immediately after the existing malformed-block check and BEFORE the capacity check: if `version != SUPPORTED_OPT_LOG_VERSION`, it returns `UnsupportedVersion` and performs NO write (fail-closed, matching the `Full`/`Multikernel` discipline exactly). New exit code `5` (distinct from `Full`=3, `Multikernel`=4, generic usage/parse/malformed=2), documented in `cli.rs`'s `LogOpt` doc comment and `main.rs`'s `run_log_opt` doc comment. New test `AT-2926` (one past the r2 spec's AT-2925 ceiling -- a QA-fix extension, not part of the original spec's AT range) in `log_opt.rs`: (1) `at_2926_version2_block_refused_source_byte_unchanged` -- reproduces the QA scenario exactly (a real parsed+lowered version:2 block, zero HIR errors) and asserts the splice core returns `UnsupportedVersion{found:2,supported:1}`, exit code 5; (2) `at_2926_version2_block_refused_file_byte_unchanged_on_disk` -- file-level `append_optimization_log`, asserts the on-disk file is byte-for-byte unchanged (md5-equivalent `assert_eq!` on the raw bytes) after the refusal; (3) `at_2926_version1_block_append_still_works` -- no-regression companion proving the fix is not over-broad. Independently re-verified end-to-end via a live `axc mcp` subprocess (JSON-RPC `append_optimization_log` against a hand-built version:2 fixture -> `error.code -32602`, file byte-unchanged) and the `axc log-opt` CLI directly (exit code 5, file byte-unchanged, JSON error body). AT-2922 (64-entry cap) and the multikernel fail-closed test were re-run and still pass unmodified -- the new check sits strictly before the capacity check and does not touch that path.

loc_budget_disclosure.why_over_cap: Not attributable to duplication (QA's own audit found none) or gold-plating beyond spec scope. Three structural drivers, each individually defensible but additive: (1) the spec's own §1.3/§1.4/§1.4a schema requires a genuinely two-mode validator (exhaustive-reject at the supported version, preserve-and-warn above it) plus a formatter that round-trips it -- this is real state-machine complexity, not boilerplate; (2) AT-2913's report-ALL parser recovery (an explicit r2 pessimistic-reviewer resolution) costs meaningfully more source than the bail-on-first-error precedent it deliberately did NOT copy; (3) the writer/MCP/CLI surface has three independent entry-point shapes (raw flags, --from-verify, --from-grid) each requiring its own resolution logic and its own AT coverage (AT-2914), which the spec's terse function-signature sketches did not fully anticipate (see the entry_from_verify_report / entry_from_grid_record deviations above). None of these individually justify a 2.9x overrun on their own, and the Coder should have flagged the cumulative total against §6 explicitly during implementation rather than only in response to QA -- that process failure (not the code itself) is the actual bug this disclosure fixes.
loc_budget_disclosure.recommendation: Not a rewrite: QA found zero duplication and the test-to-production ratio (1277:1902, ~40% test) is in line with the rest of the codebase's own discipline. Flagging for the Architect/reviewers to decide whether to retroactively widen §6's cap for FG.3-class milestones (schema-validator + writer + 3-surface CLI/MCP integration) or treat this as a one-off scope-estimation miss.
